probe: Can the serialized-prefix high-water-mark pattern preserve useful concurrency without reintroducing an arbitrary exact identity set? Compare shared CAS allocation, disjoint writer ranges, Lamport-style tuples, and closed-epoch range leasing for gap handling, retry identity stability, stale-writer exclusion, atomic effect binding, and zero-optional-quota operation.
tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST/r264 state, public primary technical sources, and direct reasoning. No O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected authority, external effect, hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package service, paid/trial API/model, manual execution, scheduler mutation, same-run wait/poll/backoff/retry, or optional second leaf.

source_observations.postgresql_sequences: PostgreSQL documents that nextval is atomic and multiuser-safe, but values are not reclaimed after abort and therefore gaps are expected. This is a direct counterexample to assuming that concurrency-safe allocation alone preserves a dense committed prefix.
source_observations.etcd_transactions: etcd documents atomic compare-guarded transactions and a single revision increment per modifying transaction, supporting the feasibility of an optimistic shared compare-and-swap commit frontier when identity advancement and durable effect-state mutation share one atomic transaction.
source_observations.lamport_ordering: Lamport logical clocks establish an ordering relation and can extend to a total order with tie-breaking, but ordering does not imply density of the set of actually issued identities; sparse tuples therefore cannot be represented exactly by one scalar membership high-water mark.
source_observations.lease_and_fencing_pattern: Chubby and ZooKeeper provide public evidence for lease/lock ownership, ordered transaction identities, and monotone sequence mechanisms; these support fencing stale writers but do not by themselves eliminate gap/accounting state for parallel preallocation.

direct_proof.shared_cas_atomic_commit: Let H be the largest semantically terminal identity. A proposer may prepare work concurrently, but commit must atomically compare H=h and write identity h+1, its terminal effect/evidence, and H=h+1. Exactly one concurrent proposer wins a given h; stale writers fail the comparison. The used/terminal identity set remains the dense prefix [0,H], so reservation membership remains exact in O(log H) state. Useful concurrency survives in preparation and optimistic contention, while the commit frontier is serialized.
direct_proof.allocation_without_atomic_effect_binding: If identity allocation is committed before the effect and the process crashes, a permanent hole appears. PostgreSQL's documented non-rollback sequence gaps instantiate this pattern. A scalar H can then mean only 'reserved at or below H', not 'effect successfully completed at or below H'. Exact duplicate non-reuse may remain conservative, but exact completion/replay semantics require extra terminal-status evidence or an independently idempotent deterministic sink.
direct_proof.disjoint_writer_ranges: Parallel ranges [a,b] make the global used set non-prefix while ranges are partially consumed. Exact membership then needs at least per-range progress/gap state. If K simultaneously active ranges is a fixed bound and each writer consumes only a contiguous local prefix, state can be O(K log H) rather than an arbitrary per-identity set. Unbounded writer/range concurrency makes K grow and loses the bounded-frontier property.
direct_proof.lamport_tuples: A Lamport tuple (clock,writer) supplies order and retry-stable identity if persisted, but the issued tuples are sparse. One global maximum cannot distinguish an issued tuple from a never-issued tuple below the maximum. Exact membership therefore needs a set, or a fixed writer universe with one contiguous high-water mark per writer, which is O(W) state and ceases to be bounded if writer identities churn without authoritative epoch closure.
direct_proof.closed_epoch_range_leasing: A bounded epoch may lease at most K disjoint ranges, fence each lease by epoch/generation, and require each writer to advance only a local contiguous prefix. While open, persist K lease descriptors/local high-water marks. After every range becomes semantically terminal through success or authoritative burn/closure, collapse the whole epoch to one global H and discard per-lease state. This preserves exact no-false-negative non-reuse with O(K log H) active state and O(log H) closed state. Exact success-vs-burn replay still requires a durable terminal distinction unless burned identities are defined as permanently consumed and retries must acquire a new identity.
direct_proof.stale_writer_exclusion: CAS revision checks or epoch/fencing tokens are sufficient to prevent a writer holding an old lease from advancing the current frontier, provided every sink mutation validates the current fence. A lease timeout alone is insufficient when a paused client can later resume against a sink that does not verify the fence.
direct_proof.atomic_side_effect_boundary: No compact identity allocator can make a non-transactional hidden side effect exactly-once by itself. Either the side effect must be in the same atomic commit as frontier advancement, expose a deterministic idempotency/resource key, or leave an unresolved child requiring additional durable outcome evidence.

single_shared_cas_frontier.useful_concurrency: medium: concurrent preparation, serialized optimistic commit
single_shared_cas_frontier.gap_handling: no committed gaps if effect and frontier advance are atomic
single_shared_cas_frontier.retry_identity_stability: strong when retry reuses the candidate identity/operation digest

unbounded_disjoint_ranges.gap_handling: unresolved without per-range terminal state or conservative burning

lamport_tuple_identity.identity_state: one scalar is insufficient; exactness requires set or fixed-writer vector
lamport_tuple_identity.exact_no_false_negative_duplicate_safety: possible with conservative max rejection or per-writer vector, but one scalar loses exact fresh acceptance
lamport_tuple_identity.retry_identity_stability: strong only if tuple is durably reused
lamport_tuple_identity.integration_cost: low for ordering, high for exact membership repair
lamport_tuple_identity.zero_optional_quota_fit: strong computationally, weak for unbounded membership state

bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.identity_state: O(K log H) while K leases are open; collapses to O(log H) after authoritative epoch closure
bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.exact_fresh_identity_acceptance: true within per-lease contiguous prefixes if terminal success/burn semantics are explicit
bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.gap_handling: epoch cannot collapse until every leased position is terminal; conservative burn is safe for non-reuse but changes replay/liveness semantics
bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.retry_identity_stability: strong within live lease/epoch; closed/burned retry needs explicit terminal rule
bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.stale_writer_exclusion: strong with epoch fencing checked at sink
bounded_closed_epoch_range_leases.zero_optional_quota_fit: strong when K is a fixed local/control bound and state rides existing lightweight repository transport

semantic_conclusion: The serialized-prefix escape hatch can preserve useful concurrency, but only by keeping the exact membership frontier structurally bounded. The strongest compact baseline is a shared CAS/transactional high-water mark: preparation may be parallel, while effect commit is serialized and atomically advances H. More commit parallelism is possible with a bounded number K of fenced epoch leases, each constrained to a local contiguous prefix; this uses O(K) frontier state and can collapse to one H after authoritative closure. Arbitrary disjoint ranges or Lamport-style sparse tuples do not preserve exact fresh-membership semantics with one scalar and reintroduce growing set/vector/gap state. Therefore concurrency itself is not the blocker; unbounded sparse concurrency is. No allocator removes the separate requirement that hidden side effects be atomically bound, deterministically idempotent, or represented by durable terminal evidence.
